title: させてもらう: receiving a caused action
summary: The causative (cause someone to do) plus もらう (receive) gives させてもらう: "receive being caused to", often a polite way to ask or to announce.

blocks.text: させてもらう looks scary, but it is built from two pieces you already know. The **causative** せる / させる means **cause** someone to do something (lesson 19), and **もらう** receives an action (lesson 49). Put them together and you get "receive someone's causing".
The causative means cause, not only make or allow

English splits "make" from "let", but the Japanese causative covers any way of causing. Even English cheats on this: "I'll **let** you know tomorrow" does not mean "allow" or "force". It means "cause you to know". Japanese says it with the causative of 知る: **知らせる**. In the same way, **聞かせる** is "cause to hear", and 読み聞かせる is to read aloud to someone. 見せる works like 見させる too: "cause to see", so "show".
Make the causative て-form and add もらう. 聞かせてもらった is "I received the teacher's causing me to hear", that is "I was told". The doer takes に, as usual with もらう.
先生に聞かせてもらった。 (I) was told by the teacher.
The one being caused is not always you. In the next sentence the glasses are what was caused to fit.

blocks.jp: 眼鏡を合わせてもらった。

blocks.text: The ending もらえますか uses もらえる, the potential of もらう: "is it possible to receive ...?" That is why it is a request. Adding させて makes it "could I receive your letting me ...?".

blocks.jp: 説明を聞かせてもらえませんか。
blocks.en: Could you tell me the explanation?

blocks.jp: ちょっと考えさせてもらえますか。
blocks.en: Could you let me think about it for a moment?

blocks.jp: 学生でも下宿させてもらえませんか。
blocks.en: Could a student lodge here too?

blocks.text: 帰らせてもらいます means "I will receive your allowing me to go home", close to English "with your permission, I'll go home now". Whether it is truly polite or a thin polite wrapper depends on tone.

blocks.jp: 明日、早く帰らせてもらいます。
blocks.en: (With your leave) I'll head home early tomorrow.

blocks.text: The humble verb **いただく** replaces もらう in very polite speech: 帰らせていただきます. You already know it from いただきます before a meal, which says "I humbly receive". It means the same thing as もらう and adds humility.

items: The causative means **cause**, which covers make, allow and arrange.
**Vさせてもらう** = receive someone's causing (me) to V.
**〜てもらえますか / もらえませんか** asks politely: can I receive …?
**いただく** is the humble form of もらう.

options: Any way of causing: make, allow, arrange
questions.note: The Japanese causative means cause, which covers make, allow and arrange.

questions.instruction: What does 知らせる mean literally?
questions.prompt: 友達に時間を知らせてもらった。
questions.note: 知らせる is the causative of 知る; "let me know" is cause to know.
questions.en: I had a friend let me know the time.

questions.instruction: What does 食べさせてもらう literally say?
questions.note: Causative て-form plus もらう: receive a causing.

questions.instruction: Which asks "may I wait (with your permission)?"
options: 待たれてもらえますか
待たせてもらえますか
questions.note: 待たせて is the causative て-form; もらえますか asks politely to receive it.

questions.instruction: Which verb replaces もらう in very polite speech?
questions.note: いただく is the humble form of もらう.

questions.prompt: 先生＿＿説明を聞かせてもらった。
questions.note: As usual with もらう, the one who does the causing takes に.
questions.en: The teacher told me the explanation.

questions.prompt: ここで少し休ませてもらえますか。
options: To rest here with the listener's permission
To offer the listener a rest
questions.note: 休ませてもらう means receiving someone's allowing me to rest.
questions.en: Could you let me rest here for a bit?

questions.prompt: ここで電話させてもらいます。
options: No, the speaker asks for permission
Yes, the speaker forces the listener
questions.note: Vさせてもらう means receiving permission, not forcing.
questions.en: With your leave, I'll make a call here.

questions.instruction: What does いただく add compared with もらう?
questions.prompt: 明日は休ませていただきます。
questions.note: いただく is the humble version of もらう.
questions.en: I'll take tomorrow off (with your permission).

questions.instruction: Who ends up seeing the photos?
questions.prompt: 友達に写真を見せてもらった。
questions.note: 見せる is like the causative of 見る: the friend causes me to see.
questions.en: I had a friend show me the photos.

questions.instruction: Say "receive permission to think about it"
questions.note: Causative て-form of 考える, then もらう.
The causative of 行く is 行かせる.

options: 帰らせていただきます
questions.note: いただく replaces もらう in humble speech.

questions.instruction: Which asks the listener to tell you something?
options: 話を聞かせてもらえませんか。
話を聞いてもらえませんか。
話を聞かせてあげませんか。
話を聞かれてもらえませんか。
questions.note: 聞かせてもらう: receive the telling.

questions.instruction: Which is the causative of 読む?
questions.note: Godan causative: あ-stem + せる.
休ませて is the causative て-form; もらえますか receives it.
questions.en: Could you let me rest here for a bit?

questions.instruction: Tap the person who gave permission
questions.note: The one who causes takes に.
questions.en: I got Mom to let me make a call.

questions.prompt: I got to use the teacher's phone.
questions.note: The causer takes に; the engine is last.
questions.en: I got the teacher to let me use the phone.

questions.prompt: I'll rest a bit today (with your leave).
questions.note: 休ませてもらいます announces an action with permission.
questions.en: I'll rest a bit today (with your leave).

questions.prompt: I had a friend show me the photos.
questions.note: 見せてもらう: receive someone's showing.
questions.en: I had a friend show me the photos.

questions.prompt: Could you let me make a call here?
options: かけさせてもらえますか
questions.note: もらえますか asks politely: can I receive …?
questions.en: Could you let me make a call here?
